subject: Rows removed when mixing geom_point and geom_path

messages.author: bfe1a38a9eb1d871
messages.subject: Rows removed when mixing geom_point and geom_path
parts:
Cheers,

I am doing a graph that mixeds points and lines together and trying to automate as much as possible. My problem is, when I try to automate it I keep gettin the "Removed 9 rows containing missing values (geom_point)." error message. Generally, the problem with such error is that we try to plot something outside its boundary, but it does not seem to be the case here. 

This code works:
names <- c(1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3)
xvals <- c(1:9)
y1vals <- c(1,2,3,10,11,12,15,16,17)
y2vals <- c(2,3,4,11,12,13,16,17,18)
p1vals <- c(1.1,2.1,3.1,11,12,13,14,15,16)
p2vals <- c(0.9,1.9,2.9,10,11,12,13,14,15)

ex_data_p1 <- data.frame(names, long=xvals, lat=p1vals)
ex_data_p1$names <- factor(ex_data_p1$names)
ex_data_p2 <- data.frame(names, long=xvals, lat=p2vals)
ex_data_p2$names <- factor(ex_data_p2$names)
ex_data_l1 <- data.frame(names, long=xvals, lat=y1vals)
ex_data_l1$names <- factor(ex_data_l1$names)
ex_data_l2 <- data.frame(names, long=xvals, lat=y2vals)
ex_data_l2$names <- factor(ex_data_l2$names)

ggplot() + 
    geom_path(data=ex_data_l1, aes(x=long, y=lat, group=names, shape='a', linetype='a', colour='a')) +
    geom_path(data=ex_data_l2, aes(x=long, y=lat, group=names, shape='b', linetype='b', colour='b')) +
    geom_point(data=ex_data_p1, aes(x=long, y=lat, group=names, shape='c', linetype='c', colour='c')) + 
    geom_point(data=ex_data_p2, aes(x=long, y=lat, group=names, shape='d', linetype='d', colour='d')) + 
    scale_color_manual('Legend', breaks=c('a', 'b', 'c', 'd'), values=rainbow(4)) + 
    scale_shape_manual('Legend', breaks=c('a', 'b', 'c', 'd'), values=c(NA, NA, 19, 19)) + 
    scale_linetype_manual('Legend', breaks=c('a', 'b', 'c', 'd'), values=c(1, 1, 0, 0))

But then I try to automate it and that's when it breaks:
my.lines <- list('a'=ex_data_l1, 'b'=ex_data_l2)
my.points <- list('c'=ex_data_p1, 'd'=ex_data_p2)
my.breaks <- c(names(my.lines), names(my.points))

graph <- ggplot()
for (l in names(my.lines)) {
    graph <- graph + geom_path(data=my.lines[[l]], aes(x=long, y=lat, group=names, shape=l, linetype=l, colour=l))
}
for (p in names(my.points)) {
    graph <- graph + geom_point(data=my.points[[p]], aes(x=long, y=lat, group=names, shape=p, linetype=p, colour=p))
}
graph <- graph + scale_color_manual('Legend', breaks=my.breaks, values=rainbow(4))
graph <- graph + scale_shape_manual('Legend', breaks=my.breaks, values=c(NA, NA, 19, 19))
graph <- graph + scale_linetype_manual('Legend', breaks=my.breaks, values=c(1, 1, 0, 0))
print(graph)

No matter how much I compare both structures, they look to me like they should get the same result. What am I doing wrong? I've got ggplot2 v.1.0.0.

Thanks in advance,

Guillermo

messages.subject: Re: Rows removed when mixing geom_point and geom_path
parts:
Hi:

When you create each subplot for lines and points, ggplot2 appears to
be retaining only the last level created. If you plot graph before
adding the manual scales, you'll see that only two levels show up in
the legend, b (from lines) and d (from points).

In the first graph, you created a factor for shape, color and linetype
on the fly by including them within aes() and then used a vector of
breaks containing the generated factor levels in each manual scale
call to inform the scales of the (generated) levels.

In the second attempt where you are pulling in separate lists of data
frames, it appears that your attempt to generate factor levels on the
fly doesn't work when trying to 'add' to the existing ggplot object
graph. The failure likely has to do with how ggplot2 trains the scales
for graph, but I don't know how it works well enough to articulate
what is going on.

One workaround is to create separate data frames for the data that
produces lines and the data that produces points, and to define a
factor with levels a-d in each, even though the
values in one will be a-b and in the other, c-d. You can then create
separate layers for the
lines and points and add the scale modifications at the end.

This doesn't quite match your first graph, but it will give you the
general idea - I'll let you figure out where I messed up. Starting
with

library(plyr)
# Create data frames by row binding the data frames
# in the two lists - it creates a new variable .id with the
# names of the list components as values/levels
DFlines <- ldply(my.lines, rbind)
DFpts <- ldply(my.points, rbind)

# Make sure that the factor .id has the same levels in each
DFlines[[".id"]] <- factor(DFlines[[".id"]], levels = my.breaks)
DFpts[[".id"]] <- factor(DFpts[[".id"]], levels = my.breaks)

# Plot
ggplot(DFlines, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = names, shape = .id,
linetype = .id, color = .id)) +
geom_path() +
geom_point(data = DFpts) +
scale_color_manual('Legend', values=rainbow(4)) +
scale_shape_manual('Legend', values=c(NA, NA, 19, 19)) +
scale_linetype_manual('Legend', values=c(1, 1, 0, 0))

I suspect that you have a broader application where the data is split
up into list components and you hoped that you could add to a ggplot
object, but I believe that if you are going to create a factor on the
fly in ggplot(), you have to do it in a single call, not a sequence of
calls. Somewhere ggplot2 has to 'know' the levels of its factors or it
can't train the legends properly. This is why I created separate data
frames for lines and points and then defined .id to have the same
levels in both data frames prior to the ggplot() call. The behavior
you experienced is an indication that ggplot2 could not train the
scales reasonably based on your inputs and reconciled the conflict by
chucking the points.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Rows removed when mixing geom_point and geom_path
parts:
Thanks a lot, Dennis.

You have guessed  right. I have different data sets for highways, power lines, railroads, etc. (geom_path) as well as powerplants, reservoirs, etc. (geom_point) that I would like to plot in a map.

Would this behaviour ("it appears that your attempt to generate factor levels on the fly doesn't work when trying to 'add' to the existing ggplot object grap") be considered as me trying to use ggplot2 beyond its boudaries or for something it was not initially conceived?

You "messed up" (if you can call it that, you have been really helpful!) in the fact that the "group=names" argument in geom_path is there to help the function differenciate between different polygons. As such, when merging 'a' and 'b' you are keeping the name '1' for both datasets, and telling the function to draw them as a single polygon which results in such weird behaviour of the red line. This could be avoided when merging the datasets by using 1a for 'a' and 1b for 'b' as group identifiers.

Here are  the lines I have modified on your example to make it fit 100% my initial plot:
ex_data_p1 <- data.frame(names=paste0(names, "p1"), long=xvals, lat=p1vals)
ex_data_p1$names <- factor(ex_data_p1$names)
ex_data_p2 <- data.frame(names=paste0(names, "p2"), long=xvals, lat=p2vals)
ex_data_p2$names <- factor(ex_data_p2$names)
ex_data_l1 <- data.frame(names=paste0(names, "l1"), long=xvals, lat=y1vals)
ex_data_l1$names <- factor(ex_data_l1$names)
ex_data_l2 <- data.frame(names=paste0(names, "l2"), long=xvals, lat=y2vals)
ex_data_l2$names <- factor(ex_data_l2$names)

Again, thanks a lot.

Guillermo
